title: Grill — Harness account stacks (round 3: boundaries + parity)
summary:
Round 2 resolved the security door: **each member keeps its own login**, and the harness account/limits stay separate. Two answers added scope that needs a precise boundary before Planning:

- **Mirror the whole config file** — but your note says *tool* auth (MCP/plugin OAuth) should travel while the *harness* login must not. `settings.json` `env` can contain `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`, which is harness auth, so the mirror needs a key-level rule.
- **Build a HOME overlay** — v1 only stacks Claude + Codex, so I need to know whether to build it for Codex now or all five HOME-override kinds, and whether it symlinks or copies.

There are also **2 behavior checks** (the circular train cap, and the CLI/indicator/parity defaults) and **11 one-click defaults** at the end.
proven: Round 2 settled: **own login per member**, never copy harness credentials; **Claude + Codex only** (OpenCode out of v1); **forward within a task, circular wrap at the end, one full lap cap**; **status divider** for the swap notice; **keep queued follow-ups, cancel cards, name abandoned agents**; **next-turn lifecycle**; **preserve the conversation on a manual stack-internal switch**; **hidden-tagged continuation prompt** with no product name; **proactive + reactive selection**; **account-global cooldown**; **no hard stack cap but a virtualized UI and a warning above 10**; **opt-in by creating a stack**; **no per-task opt-out**.

sections.title: Boundaries for the two new scope items
sections.intro: These pin what "mirror everything" and the HOME overlay actually mean, so the plan does not guess.

questions.title: `mirror-everything` copies `settings.json` `env`, which can contain harness API keys. Should the mirror strip harness-auth keys?
questions.why: Your round-2 note says the harness login/account must stay separate so each account has its own limits. A copied `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` makes the backup use the primary's account and share its quota, which is exactly the separation you asked for. MCP/plugin OAuth tokens are different: they authenticate a tool, not the harness.
questions.context: `settings.json` is already one of the user-level files Agetor discovers. Its `env` block is a common place to put provider keys. The mirror can copy the file but filter the `env` keys: strip the known harness-auth keys, keep MCP/plugin tokens and ordinary env vars. The alternative is to copy `env` verbatim, which reintroduces the same-account problem at the config layer.

evidence.label: settings.json is a user-level capability file
provider keys in the process env already leak into every harness
the investigation's warning
evidence.code: Provider env vars (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, …) set in Agetor's own process environment are **inherited by every harness** unless the harness's env overrides them. This can silently make every account use one API key — a cross-account auth leak to account for when defining "auth tokens preserved".

options.label: Strip harness-auth keys, keep tool auth and other env
options.description: Copy `env` but remove the known harness-auth keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY`, …). Keep MCP/plugin OAuth and ordinary env vars.
options.consequence: Honors "tool auth travels, harness login does not". Needs a maintained key list and a test that the backup never inherits a harness key.

options.label: Copy `env` as-is
options.description: The backup inherits every env var in the primary's settings, including any harness API key.
options.consequence: Simplest, but the backup may silently use the primary's key and share its quota — the same-account problem you just ruled out for credentials.

options.label: Do not copy `env` at all
options.description: The backup keeps its own env; only the rest of the settings file is mirrored.
options.consequence: Safest for auth, but tooling that relies on non-auth env vars loses them.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option that matches your note: MCP/plugin auth travels, the harness account does not.

questions.title: When should the mirror run?
questions.why: A one-time copy at stack creation is stale; a live merge on every spawn can overwrite backup-local changes without review; a manual Sync is predictable but easy to forget before a swap.
questions.context: The owner chose `mirror-everything`, so the question is cadence and conflict resolution, not whether. The backup is about to run at swap time; that is when it needs the primary's current MCP servers, skills and tool auth. A merge that keeps backup-only entries and lets the primary win on shared keys is the least surprising.

options.label: At stack creation and before each swap
options.description: Mirror when the stack is created and re-sync immediately before a swap. The primary wins for entries it defines; entries that exist only on the backup are kept.
options.consequence: The backup is current at the moment it is needed, and a backup-local extra is not deleted. A swap takes a little longer while the mirror runs.

options.label: Only on a manual "Sync from primary"
options.description: Nothing is copied until the user presses the button in Settings.
options.consequence: Most predictable, but a stale backup can miss a newly added MCP server at the worst moment.

options.label: Merge on every spawn
options.description: Every turn reads the primary's config and merges it into the backup's launch.
options.consequence: Always current, but a primary change takes effect with no review and can overwrite a backup-local customization mid-task.

recommendation.reason: It keeps the backup current at the only moment that matters (the swap) while keeping the sync observable and repeatable.

questions.title: What should the HOME overlay share, and for which kinds?
questions.why: The overlay is a new, security-sensitive subsystem: it puts links to the user's `.ssh`, `.gitconfig`, `gh` and npm config inside an agent-writable home. v1 only stacks Claude + Codex, so building and testing all five HOME-override kinds now is scope the feature cannot exercise yet.
questions.context: The owner chose the overlay in round 2. Codex is the only v1 kind that overrides HOME; cursor, fx, antigravity and opencode are out of v1. The overlay must not merge the CLI's own state dirs (`CODEX_HOME`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.fx`, the OpenCode XDG dirs) — those stay per-account. A fixed allowlist is predictable and testable; a full-home symlink is closer to "same environment" but hard to enumerate and easy to get wrong.

evidence.label: codex re-homes HOME
the investigation calls the overlay a separate, broad feature
evidence.code: - **HOME overlay for HOME-override kinds:** a per-account HOME that symlinks/copies standard dotfiles (`~/.gitconfig`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh`, …) but keeps the CLI's own state dirs separate. This is a separate, broad feature; without it, mixing built-in and alias accounts changes the tool environment.

options.label: Codex only, fixed allowlist, symlinked
options.description: Implement the overlay for Codex in v1: symlink `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.gitignore_global`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.npmrc` and `~/.netrc` into the account's home; keep `CODEX_HOME` per-account. Apply it only to accounts that are stack members, so existing aliases keep today's behavior.
options.consequence: The v1 kind gets working git/ssh/gh without changing any other account. A generic module can add the other four when they join a stack.

options.label: All five HOME-override kinds now
options.description: Same allowlist, applied to Codex, Cursor, fx, Antigravity and OpenCode.
options.consequence: Fixes the limitation everywhere, but four of the five have no v1 stack support and cannot be exercised end-to-end. Larger test matrix.

options.label: Codex only, copy instead of symlink
options.description: Copy the allowlisted files into each account home.
options.consequence: No live links, but the copies go stale and a copied `.ssh` key or `gh` token sits in another home.

options.label: Symlink the whole home except the CLI state dirs
options.description: Closest to the real environment; everything not owned by the CLI is visible.
options.consequence: Most faithful and the hardest to secure: enumerating what to exclude is error-prone, and a missed exclusion can merge CLI state or credentials between accounts.

recommendation.reason: It delivers the overlay for the only v1 kind that needs it, with a small, testable allowlist and no behavior change for existing aliases.

questions.title: Confirm the circular train: forward, wrap to the head at the end, and stop after one full lap?
questions.why: Your round-2 note adds a wrap that the original "forward only" option did not describe. The exact algorithm decides whether a run can loop forever and when the all-exhausted pause starts.
questions.context: Your note: "it must return to the primary only if the last stack account reaches the limit, then a natural swap to the beginning of the stack happens, ie. going to the primary. We just need to make sure that if all accounts are tried in a run, to avoid running the train in loop, we must pause, as a cap." The algorithm below implements exactly that: move forward on each limit; when the last member limits, wrap to the head if it is available; track the members tried in this run; once every member has been tried without a successful turn, stop and use the all-exhausted behavior (auto-retry at the earliest reset, cap 3).

options.label: Circular with a one-lap cap
options.description: Forward on each limit; wrap to the head when the last member limits; stop after every member has been tried once in this run and fall into the all-exhausted pause.
options.consequence: Matches your note and cannot loop. Needs a per-run `triedMembers` set and a clear "one full lap" status line.

options.label: Forward only, block at the end
options.description: No wrap; when the last member limits, go straight to the all-exhausted pause.
options.consequence: Simpler, but does not return to the primary when its quota has reset.

options.label: Return to the primary only after its reset
options.description: Wait for the primary's `resetsAtMs` and return then, rather than wrapping when the last member limits.
options.consequence: Most primary-first, but adds a mid-task timer and can leave the task idle while a healthy backup is available.

recommendation.reason: It is the literal reading of your note, and the one-lap cap is the loop guard you asked for.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Parity and integration defaults. One click each, or override with what it should be.

questions.title: CLI and bundle parity in v1

recommendation.value: `agetor harness stack` create/list/edit/remove, and `ls`/`show`/`logs` show the active member and the swap line; the TUI shows the active member/position. Stacks are machine-local and not exported in bundles; a profile still binds an account and the stack follows implicitly.
recommendation.reason: CLI users need CRUD and visibility; a bundle cannot carry credentials or homes, so exporting a stack would be a false promise.

questions.title: Where the active account is visible

recommendation.value: Run panel shows `account · position/count`; the task card shows a small stack badge; a toast/OS notification fires on a swap when the window is unfocused; the topbar keeps one usage chip per account in v1 (no grouping).
recommendation.reason: The run panel is where the task is watched, the toast covers the unfocused case, and grouping the topbar is a separate layout change.

recommendation.value: User drag order in the stack editor; a new member appends at the end; selection starts at the first enabled, logged-in member and follows the order.
recommendation.reason: Predictable and inspectable; the drag order is the only thing the user has to reason about.

recommendation.value: At creation and before each swap: hard-block on a different kind or the same effective home; warn on not installed, not logged in, or the task's model not offered. A hard block is only for conditions that make failover meaningless.
recommendation.reason: The hard blocks are permanent; the warnings are transient and should not prevent saving a stack.

questions.title: Manual Run on a cooling account

recommendation.value: A manual Run or message on a cooling-down account forces it; automatic selection skips it.
recommendation.reason: The user's explicit action wins; the cooldown is advisory.

recommendation.value: A swap is a new run row on the same task with the new member in `runs.agent`; Agetor's `run_events` transcript stays canonical; the old run is marked failed with a swap reason and its failure toast is suppressed.
recommendation.reason: Preserves the one-in-flight-run invariant and makes the swap auditable in history.

recommendation.value: Pipeline step tasks inherit failover automatically; the implicit model needs no pipeline format change.
recommendation.reason: Each step already has its own task and agent profile, so the stack follows the step's account.

recommendation.value: Warn at stack creation when process-level provider keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) would be inherited by every member; do not scrub them in v1.
recommendation.reason: The leak is real, but changing env inheritance could break users who rely on it; the mirror's `env` filter is the v1 protection.

recommendation.value: `Switched to <account> — <reason>. Continuing from the transferred conversation.` No product name in the text.
recommendation.reason: Names the account (never an email or token), the reason, and what happens next; matches your note "just don't mention Agetor".

recommendation.value: `docs/plans/harness-account-stacks.md` (written from this record) is the binding spec; no separate PRD. The investigation brief stays as evidence.
recommendation.reason: The requirement lives outside the repo; the plan is the path a reviewer can open.

recommendation.value: Add a Codex HOME-overlay test (git config visible in the backup) and a mirror test (MCP/plugin auth copied, harness login never copied, harness-auth env keys stripped). OpenCode is out of v1, so its adapter test is dropped.
recommendation.reason: The two round-2 scope additions need their own proof, and the v1 kind set is now fixed.
